title: spec: ImportRequest.matchFields describe does not say a multi-value or structured field is refused as a match key
body:
domain:server#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgXcN9HaZYSEUdJWEjw

Filing gate: ① follow-up owed by landed work (#27465, PR #27562), raised as should-fix ③.4 by contract review 6497763460 and carried by the seat. reach: the published schema's `describe` text (`ImportRequestSchema.matchFields`, `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` ~L295-306) ships in the JSON schema and the generated API reference, so a caller reading it today is not told about a 400 the server now answers.
Business reason: an integrator or an AI author building an import request picks `matchFields` from the describe. Once #27562 lands, `update` / `upsert` with a match key naming a field stored as a list or a structured value (a `multiple: true` lookup / user / select / file, a multiselect / checkboxes / tags field, or a json / address / location / other JSON-stored field) is refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` before any row. The describe says nothing about it, so the caller learns it only from the refusal.
Reader who acts: the `domain:spec` lane, on its next touch of `export.zod.ts` (one sentence in the `matchFields` describe; `insert` is not judged).
Dedupe (open AND closed): titles of the last 100 issues and PRs matched against "matchFields", "match key" and "match-key": 2 hits, #27562 (the fix PR) and #27567 (the ui half), neither is the describe; #27465 is the parent.

Back-link: #27465 · ⛔ Not a claim. Grading is triage's.

## Expected

The `matchFields` describe adds one sentence: in `update` / `upsert`, a key naming a multi-value or structured field (the spec's own arbiters `isMultiValueField` and `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES`) is refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, naming each such field; a programmatic `runImport` caller (the connector pull) gets per-row `VALIDATION_ERROR` instead. `content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` already states both (PR #27562).
